name: Web Components | a11y-elements
tagline: Framework-agnostic accessibility Custom Elements: a behavior layer for real markup, not a themed UI kit.

keyPoints: About thirty elements: form controls (input, select, checkbox and radio groups, switch, file input…), links, pictures, tabs, and overlays (modal, drawer, popover, tooltip, dropdown, context menu, snackbar…).
Light DOM only: elements enhance the consumer's own markup, styled with the consumer's own CSS.
Every visual value is a CSS custom property, with an opt-in dark theme.
Usable with a bundler, or with no build step through per-element browser bundles.
Published on npm, used by this portfolio and other Nutin projects.

popTagline: Built to stop rewriting the same accessibility behavior in every project.

overview.mainContent: a11y-elements packages the accessibility behavior I kept rewriting from project to project: focus management, keyboard interaction, ARIA wiring and live announcements. Each element is a native Custom Element that works with any framework, or none.
keyPoints: Native Custom Elements, with no runtime dependency.
Overlays with focus traps, scroll lock, stacking and close reasons.
Built-in strings (e.g. "opens in new tab") translatable in a single call.
A built-in sanitizer for markup passed to elements.
Tested with Vitest and jsdom (700+ tests).

purpose.title: Purpose
keyPoints: To make accessible behavior the default rather than an afterthought in each project.
To stay independent from any framework, Nutin included.
To leave visual design to each project.

constraints.title: Constraints
keyPoints: Light DOM: no Shadow DOM, so the consumer's markup and CSS stay in control.
Real elements: real links, buttons and inputs, never imitations.
Load only what you use: one entry per element.

choices.title: Enhancing real elements
choices.mainContent: Most elements enhance children written by the author (a link, a select, a picture) instead of generating their own markup. A MutationObserver keeps ARIA attributes in sync when those children change, with guarded writes so the observer never loops.

choices.title: Everything themable
choices.mainContent: Each component reads its values from its own custom properties, falling back to about a dozen global semantic variables, then to the shipped default.
choices.after: A few variables are enough to theme every element.

choices.title: Standalone bundles that cooperate
choices.mainContent: Browser bundles share their common code through chunk files, and page-wide state (ids, strings, open overlays) lives on a global store, so separately loaded bundles work together.

challenges.title: Default colors that pass WCAG
challenges.mainContent: Status colors were reviewed against WCAG AA contrast with their text, and a test now checks every default pair.

challenges.title: Focus traps that behave like native Tab
challenges.mainContent: Inside a focus trap, each radio group is a single Tab stop, as it is natively.

keyPoints: Accessibility is mostly behavior: focus, keyboard and announcements.
A small public API is easier to keep accessible than a large one.
Tests are the most reliable record of ARIA expectations.
